video:video.video:title: Stephanie Dailey saved over $20,000 in taxes in her first year
video:video.video:description: Stephanie and her husband are software engineers with five kids and over $300,000 in W-2 income, plus contract work from the consulting business they run. In her first year in the Legacy Wealth Blueprint she opened separate business bank accounts, started keeping real books, captured $27,000 in startup costs, deducted over $60,000 of bridge loan mortgage interest and put her kids on payroll through Gusto.

video:video.video:title: Albert put his net worth growth at 25% and cut his home insurance in half
video:video.video:description: Albert is an ER physician in California who finished residency in 2021 with about $5,000 in a Roth and a combined tax bracket he puts at almost 50%. In the Legacy Wealth Blueprint he started tax loss harvesting, changed how he uses his HSA, opened a backdoor Roth IRA, took his portfolio off professional management and formed the entity for a new telemedicine clinic.

video:video.video:title: Abigail calculated just under $100,000 in first-year ROI
video:video.video:description: Abigail left oil and gas in the summer of 2023 and runs the numbers for her own family and her parents. She finished the Legacy Wealth Blueprint modules inside the first month, rebuilt the entity and estate work she had set up badly eight years earlier, took a weekly coaching call with her coach Brandon, recategorized every transaction as business or not business, and went under contract on her first property.

video:video.video:title: Shawn came for the tax knowledge his CPAs were not giving him
video:video.video:description: Shawn is a business owner who already held Airbnbs, rentals, crypto and stocks. What he did not have was the tax side, and he says he was struggling to get useful help from CPAs.

video:video.video:title: Rob clears more than $10,000 a month from two Airbnb properties in Louisville and St. Simons Island
video:video.video:description: Rob was a sales professional with two young kids when he chose the arbitrage model over buying so he would not tie up capital in down payments. He runs two properties, one in Louisville, Kentucky and one on St.

video:video.video:title: Gary makes $35,000 a month from seven Austin properties, three years in
video:video.video:description: Gary was a marketing executive at eBay and Chegg before building an Airbnb business in Austin, Texas. He runs seven properties with an eighth in progress, targets $10,000 gross and $5,000 to $6,000 net per property, and holds a 50% margin across the portfolio.

video:video.video:title: Michael locked up two Space Coast deals in one week and projects $12,000 a month
video:video.video:description: Michael is a serial entrepreneur who sold five companies before moving into Airbnb arbitrage on the Space Coast of Florida. He locked up two deals in one week, went from joining the program to a live listing in six weeks, and took his first booking five minutes after the listing went live.

video:video.video:title: Brian O'Leary makes $1,500 to $2,000 a month from one Iowa property
video:video.video:description: Brian works full time in IT and added an Airbnb arbitrage unit in Iowa rather than buying another property. The four-bedroom historic home sleeps ten, went live in February and was cash flow positive by March at $1,500 to $2,000 a month after expenses.

video:video.video:title: Grayson Nichols hit 75% occupancy and $3,500 a month by his third month near Austin
video:video.video:description: Grayson is a remote IT worker who took six months to work through the program before going live in July 2023 with one property near Austin, Texas. Profit went from $1,000 in September to $3,500 in October at 75% occupancy, with most bookings coming from VRBO and a booking horizon stretching six months out.

video:video.video:title: Marchia and Cash took one Atlanta property from $2,400 in February to $6,000 in April
video:video.video:description: Brothers Marchia, 27, and Cash, 23, built an Airbnb arbitrage business in downtown Atlanta, one of the most crowded markets in the country. Their first property went from $2,400 in February to $4,950 in March and over $6,000 in April with a week still open, against $3,200 a month in rent, and AirDNA puts the annual run rate at $70,000 to $75,000.

video:video.video:title: Tom booked $25,000 in his first two weeks live on the Chesapeake Bay
video:video.video:description: Tom was a Capital One executive with a software engineering background and no rental experience when he launched his first Airbnb on the Chesapeake Bay in Maryland.

video:video.video:title: Kiana left a ten year finance career and makes $3,200 a month from two Scottsdale properties
video:video.video:description: Kiana spent more than a decade in finance and six months researching short-term rental rules across the country before acting. She now runs two properties ten minutes apart in Scottsdale, Arizona for $3,200 a month in combined cash flow, quit her job three months after joining, and has cut weekly management from ten hours to four.

video:video.video:title: Dustin Cotton makes $6,000 a month from two Texas properties, four weeks from joining to first lease
video:video.video:description: Dustin came from corporate sales with no rental experience and runs two lakefront properties in Texas for about $6,000 a month in cash flow. He spent three weeks on research without making a call, found his first markets were hostile or crowded, then lined up five interested landlords across one weekend of eight to ten hour calling days.

video:video.video:title: Lindsay Fischer and her husband booked $17,500 in 14 days live in the North Carolina mountains
video:video.video:description: Lindsay and her husband moved from nonprofit and 9-to-5 work into Airbnb arbitrage in the Western North Carolina mountains, thirty minutes outside Asheville. They went from first landlord contact to a signed contract in 21 days and secured the property on their fourth call.

video:video.video:title: Hampton booked $20,000 in his first month on his parents' lakefront home
video:video.video:description: Hampton is a process engineer who started with his parents' lakefront property, showing them a projection of what the weekends they were not using could earn. The listing booked $20,000 within weeks and over $30,000 across four months.

video:video.video:title: Andrew Wolf averages $1,500 a month from a Tulum Airbnb he runs remotely from the United States
video:video.video:description: Andrew came from hotel management and runs a single arbitrage property in Tulum, Mexico entirely from the United States. Year one averaged about $1,500 a month across seasons, with nightly rates swinging from $400 in high season to $100 in the summer, and he projects $2,500 a month in year two once the new airport opens.

video:video.video:title: Christopher Bamford makes $1,700 a month in Louisiana after 50 to 70 landlord calls
video:video.video:description: Christopher started out buying at garage sales to run an eBay business and could never find a way into real estate with the capital normally required. He made 50 to 70 landlord calls and lost several deals where the numbers did not work before signing a three-year lease on a Louisiana property that now returns over $1,700 a month.

video:video.video:title: Kirk hit 87% occupancy and $5,500 in March from one California property while nursing full time
video:video.video:description: Kirk is a full-time nurse in California who had never started a business before. He projected $2,000 a month conservatively and the property has run ahead of that, at $5,500 in March on 87% occupancy and over $4,400 in April on 70%.

video:video.video:title: Sunny makes $2,000 to $5,000 a month from one Houston townhouse near the Texas Medical Center
video:video.video:description: Sunny is a respiratory therapist who runs a five-bedroom, four-storey townhouse six minutes from the Texas Medical Center in Houston. He found Preston Seo through Instagram reels, spent four months from Thanksgiving to a March launch, and now holds a baseline above $2,000 a month with a peak of $5,216 during a Taylor Swift concert month.
